caption: Figure 14.1: Co-moving wakefield geometry, the Panofsky–Wenzel 3×3 stencil, and impedance post-processing in WakeSolver. Left: an ultrarelativistic source bunch q_1 with line density λ(s) travels along +z at v = βc at transverse offset r_{⊥,1} = (x_1, y_1) through a structure of length L = z_max − z_min, followed at co-moving lag s = vt − z by a witness charge q_2 at r_{⊥,2} = (x_2, y_2). Centre: WakeSolver records only E_z inside a 3×3 cell tube around (x_test, y_test) and recovers W_⊥ via the Panofsky–Wenzel theorem. Right: Fourier transformation and normalization by the bunch spectrum λ̃(ω) yield Z_∥(ω), Z_⊥(ω) and the loss factor k_loss.
visual_intent:
Textbook-quality scientific schematic for a computational electromagnetics user manual. Flat vector style on a white background, high contrast, thin dark outlines, generous whitespace, sans-serif labels. Colour code used in every figure: longitudinal fields, TM quantities and dispersion-free curves in blue, transverse fields, TE quantities and source/witness beam items in orange, exact/structural items and PEC walls in dark grey, plasma/material and integration items in green, spurious Cherenkov or unstable items in red. Colourblind-safe. Every label must be spelled exactly as listed in this brief; mathematical symbols must be typeset correctly (hats, tildes, subscripts, transposes). Do not add any number, value, equation, software name, product name, logo, watermark or title that is not listed in this brief. Prefer fewer, larger labels over many small ones. No 3D photorealism, no cartoon characters, no hand-drawn or xkcd style.

Three panels side by side. LEFT PANEL (45% width) 'Co-moving wake integration': an axisymmetric cavity with beam pipes extending horizontally from 'z_min' to 'z_max' (bracket below labelled 'L = z_max − z_min', walls in dark grey). Moving right along '+z' at speed 'v = βc' is an orange Gaussian ellipse labelled 'source bunch q_1, λ(s)' at offset 'r_{⊥,1} = (x_1, y_1)'. Trailing behind by a horizontal double-headed arrow labelled 's = vt − z (s > 0 behind)' is an orange dot 'witness q_2' at 'r_{⊥,2} = (x_2, y_2)', flying along a green shaded horizontal tube labelled '3×3 E_z integration tube: t = (z + s)/v'. Below: 'W_∥(x_2, y_2, s) = −(1/q_1) ∫_{z_min}^{z_max} E_z(x_2, y_2, z, t=(z+s)/v) dz'. CENTRE PANEL (25% width) 'Panofsky–Wenzel 3×3 stencil': a 3×3 square grid of cells in the (x, y) cross-section centred on '(x_test, y_test)' (blue dot at centre and its neighbours carrying 'E_z' only), with horizontal and vertical finite-difference arrows labelled '∇_{⊥,2}'. Below: 'W_⊥ = ∇_{⊥,2} ∫_{-∞}^s W_∥(s′) ds′' and badge 'records only E_z'. RIGHT PANEL (30% width) 'Impedance & loss factor': a vertical flow of three boxes from 'W_∥(s), W_⊥(s) [V/pC]' → arrow labelled 'FFT / (v λ̃(ω))' → 'Z_∥(ω), Z_⊥(ω) [Ω]' and 'k_loss = ∫ W_∥(s) λ(s) ds = (1/π) ∫_0^∞ Re Z_∥(ω) |λ̃(ω)|² dω'.
target_diagram_desc0:
The figure is a textbook-quality scientific schematic rendered in a flat vector style on a pure white background. It features high contrast, thin dark outlines, generous whitespace, and sans-serif typography. The diagram adheres strictly to a specific colourblind-safe colour code: longitudinal fields/TM quantities in blue, transverse fields/TE quantities and beam items in orange, structural/exact items and PEC walls in dark grey, and integration/material items in green. The figure is divided into three side-by-side panels.

**Left Panel (45% width):**
This panel illustrates the "Co-moving wake integration". 
- **Structure:** A horizontal axisymmetric cavity with beam pipes extending from the left to the right is drawn with dark grey walls. Below the cavity, a horizontal bracket marks the length, labelled exactly "L = z_max − z_min" in dark grey.
- **Source Bunch:** Inside the cavity, moving to the right along the "+z" direction, is an orange Gaussian-shaped ellipse. It has an orange velocity vector arrow labelled "v = βc". Adjacent to the ellipse is the text "source bunch q_1, λ(s)" and its transverse offset is indicated with the label "r_{⊥,1} = (x_1, y_1)" in orange.
- **Witness:** Trailing behind the source bunch to the left is a small orange dot. An orange horizontal double-headed arrow connects the center of the source bunch to this dot, labelled "s = vt − z (s > 0 behind)". The dot is labelled "witness q_2" and is positioned at "r_{⊥,2} = (x_2, y_2)".
- **Integration Path:** The witness dot flies along a green-shaded, semi-transparent horizontal tube that runs through the cavity. The green tube is labelled "3×3 E_z integration tube: t = (z + s)/v".
- **Equation:** At the bottom of this panel, the longitudinal wake potential equation is typeset cleanly: "W_∥(x_2, y_2, s) = −(1/q_1) ∫_{z_min}^{z_max} E_z(x_2, y_2, z, t=(z+s)/v) dz". The E_z and W_∥ parts are in blue, integration components in green, and coordinate/beam parameters in orange.

**Centre Panel (25% width):**
This panel details the "Panofsky–Wenzel 3×3 stencil".
- **Grid:** A crisp 3×3 square grid of cells is drawn in thin dark grey lines, representing the (x, y) cross-section. 
- **Nodes:** The central cell contains a blue dot labelled "(x_test, y_test)". The adjacent neighbour cells in the grid also contain smaller blue dots, with the text "E_z" indicating they only carry the longitudinal electric field. 
- **Vectors:** Orange horizontal and vertical arrows span across the grid cells to denote finite-difference operations, explicitly labelled with the transverse gradient symbol "∇_{⊥,2}".
- **Equations & Badges:** Below the grid, an equation is written: "W_⊥ = ∇_{⊥,2} ∫_{-∞}^s W_∥(s′) ds′". W_⊥ and ∇_{⊥,2} are in orange, while W_∥ is in blue and the integral in green. Next to the equation is a neatly bordered badge stating "records only E_z".

**Right Panel (30% width):**
This panel shows the "Impedance & loss factor" calculation via a vertical flowchart.
- **Flowchart Top:** A rectangular box contains the wake potentials in the time domain: "W_∥(s), W_⊥(s) [V/pC]" (with W_∥ in blue and W_⊥ in orange).
- **Process Arrow:** A vertical arrow points downwards from this box, overlaid with the mathematical operation text: "FFT / (v λ̃(ω))".
- **Flowchart Bottom Elements:** The arrow points to two resulting text groups. The first reads "Z_∥(ω), Z_⊥(ω) [Ω]", with Z_∥ in blue and Z_⊥ in orange. Below this, a final equation block calculates the loss factor: "k_loss = ∫ W_∥(s) λ(s) ds = (1/π) ∫_0^∞ Re Z_∥(ω) |λ̃(ω)|² dω". The mathematical symbols are properly typeset with correct hats, tildes, subscripts, and absolute value bars. 

There are no 3D effects, shadows, cartoon elements, hand-drawn aesthetics, or extraneous titles/watermarks anywhere in the image.

1. **Mathematical Accuracy**: In the Right Panel, the first integral for the loss factor equation $k_{\text{loss}}$ is missing its limits. To accurately reflect the Methodology Section, it should include the full range: $\int_{-\infty}^\infty W_\parallel(s)\lambda(s) ds$.
2. **Legend Management**: The detailed description contains a paragraph explicitly acting as a text-based legend explaining the entire color-coding scheme. This has been excised in accordance with the presentation rules.
